scope: synthetic orchestration benchmark only; no production worker or mission mutation semantics changed
problem: The existing critical-path benchmark assumes independent missions can always run concurrently. That can overstate expected Qubes performance when a finite worker fleet has overlapping capability coverage.

independent_reviews.reason: Schedules the actual runtime DAG against explicit worker capability sets, respects dependency completion, and makes worker contention visible instead of inferring it from DAG width alone.
Rejects duplicate worker identities, empty capability sets, and missions with no capable worker. Deterministic tie-breaking keeps benchmark evidence replayable.

Adds no qrexec traffic, daemon, database, worker process, or production state. Runtime cost is local and small for the current mission graphs, while directly exposing queue delay and fleet utilization.

approaches.name: unlimited-critical-path-only
approaches.correctness: good for theoretical DAG latency, weak for finite worker capacity
approaches.result: rejected as the sole readiness signal

approaches.name: deterministic-worker-fleet-list-scheduling
approaches.correctness: models dependency readiness, worker availability, capability coverage, queue delay, and constrained latency
approaches.latency: offline computation only; no transport overhead
approaches.regression_risk: low because production semantics are unchanged

approaches.name: benchmark-through-production-worker-scheduler
approaches.correctness: highest fidelity once a stable Qubes worker environment exists
approaches.robustness: couples benchmark failures to transport, leases, and VM availability
approaches.result: deferred until Qubes execution evidence exists

required: independent specialist workers preserve theoretical fan-out latency
shared specialist worker exposes contention and fails strict readiness thresholds
qa.release_note: Hosted GitHub runner provisioning remains a separate blocker. This benchmark can be exercised by local/Qube QA but does not replace independent hosted CI.

failure_lessons: DAG peak concurrency is not equivalent to deployable worker capacity.
Capability topology must be part of performance evidence before sizing Qubes workers.
A benchmark that ignores queue delay can report a speedup that disappears when specialists share workers.
